title: ～っぽい — ～-ish / tends to be ～
summary: A suffix added to nouns or verb stems that makes an i-adjective meaning “has the feel of ～, ～-ish” or “tends to ～.” It often shows a feature that is slightly negative or less than ideal. Casual.

patterns.gloss: has the feel of the noun (油っぽい、子どもっぽい)

patterns.form: 動詞ます形（語幹）＋っぽい
patterns.gloss: tends to do (忘れっぽい、怒りっぽい)

body.p: After a noun it means “close to ～ in feel” (油っぽい, 子どもっぽい, 灰色っぽい). After a verb stem it means “tends to ～” (忘れっぽい, 飽きっぽい, 怒りっぽい). Both conjugate like i-adjectives (忘れっぽくなった).

It often carries a slightly negative impression. 子どもっぽい is a criticism: childish for an adult. With colors it can be neutral (白っぽい服). For praise use らしい instead: 〜らしい means “typical of / worthy of ～” in a good sense, unlike っぽい.

examples.ja: この料理（りょうり）は少（すこ）し油（あぶら）っぽい。
examples.tr: This dish is a bit oily.

examples.ja: 最近（さいきん）の父（ちち）は、少（すこ）し忘（わす）れっぽくなった。
examples.romaji: Saikin no chichi wa, sukoshi wasureppoku natta.
examples.tr: Lately my father has become a bit forgetful.
examples.note: Verb stem + っぽい: tends to forget.

examples.ja: 空（そら）が灰色（はいいろ）っぽくなって、雨（あめ）が近（ちか）い。
examples.romaji: Sora ga haiirobboku natte, ame ga chikai.
examples.tr: The sky has turned grayish; rain is coming soon.
examples.note: With a color, it is neutral: “grayish.”

pitfalls: It is hard to use as praise. 男らしい and 男っぽい mean different things.
Attach it directly to the noun or stem. “忘れるっぽい” is wrong.
